sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of October, 2024 The United India Insurance Company Limited has come up in appeal against the award dated 25.02.2020 in O.P(MV) No.316/2019 on the files of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The facts, in brief, for the disposal of the aforesaid appeal are as follows:
The claimants are the legal heirs of one Sri.Milanth, who met with a road accident on 3 1 . 0 5 . 2 0 1 8 a t 6 . 4 5 p . m . W h i l e h e w a s r i d i n g m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Regn.No.KL-43/K-7442 along Palluruthy- Thoppumpady road, another motorcycle bearing Regn.No.KL-7/AW- 6586 driven by one Sri.Nibin dashed into the motorcycle driven by Sri.Milanth.
Due to the impact, Sri.Milanth fell down and sustained fatal injuries.
Though he was taken to Goutham Hospital, Panayapally, succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.

The appellant appeared and filed a written statement stating that 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KL-7/AW-6586 and in fact, negligence was on the side of the deceased himself.
The Insurance policy with respect to the vehicle was admitted.
On behalf of the claimants, Exts.A1 to A9 were marked and on the side of the Insurance company Exts.B1 and B2 were marked.

On the basis of the material evidence on record, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
"1. Whether Mr.Milanth died in a road traffic accident as alleged?
2. What is the cause of accident?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to get compensation?

If so, for what amount,
from who?
4. Reliefs and costs?"
3. The Tribunal based on Ext.A4 Final report and Ext.A2 Postmortem Certificate proceeded to hold that the deceased met with road traffic accident and succumbed to injuries.

However, since the insurance company raised a question regarding the negligence on the part of the deceased Milanth,
the Tribunal proceeded to consider the said question.

The Tribunal, after analyzing the evidence,
held that 25% contributory negligence has to be attributed to the deceased who 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 drove the vehicle bearing Registration No. KL-43/K-7442.
Aggrieved by the said fixation, the insurance company has come up in appeal stating that 75% of the contributory negligence ought to have been fixed by the Tribunal against the deceased.

sentences.text: Heard Sri. Rajan P Kaliyath, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company and Smt.T. Manasy, the learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3 and also perused the records and the award passed by the Tribunal.

5. On an anxious consideration of the evidence on record, it is to be noted that the findings of the Tribunal are based on Ext.A4 Final Report of charge in Crime No.2548/2018 of City Traffic West Police Station, Kochi City.

entities.text: City Traffic West Police Station, Kochi City
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The final report has Charge "A" and Charge "B".
On the conclusion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer had concluded that the accident occurred because of the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KL-7/AW-6586.
The Tribunal relying on the said report proceeded to fix 25% of the contributory negligence on the side of the deceased Milanth.

The basis of such finding was that the width of the road where the 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 accident occurred is 9.5 metres, whereas the accident spot is at a place 5.15 metres from the margin, which indicates that the deceased drove the vehicle in such a manner transgressing the middle line.
However, the only ground on which 50% of negligence was not attributed to the deceased was that there was no evidence to show that overtaking was prohibited on the said road.
In essence, the finding of the Tribunal is purely on the assumption that the deceased had transgressed into the portion of the road and thereby, the said act was the prime cause for the accident.
Pertinently, it has to be said that the Tribunal completely ignored the charge against the "A" vehicle.

When impeccable evidence was available in the form of the final report stating that the accused, the rider of the motor vehicle bearing Regn.No.KL-7/AW-6586 drew the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, on what basis the Tribunal fixed the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased,
cannot be comprehended.
6. Be that as it may, the Tribunal, in its wisdom, thought that 25% of the contributory negligence should be fixed against the deceased Milanth.

Perhaps because of these findings of the Tribunal 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 that the Insurance company has come in appeal pointing out that the Tribunal ought to have fixed 75% contributory negligence against the deceased Milanth.
7. Perhaps, had the claimants come up in appeal against the particular finding of the Tribunal fixing contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, things would have been different.

8. The concept of negligence and its types and its composite and contributory were discussed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Laxman Iyer and Another [2003 (8) SCC 731] and the same reads as follows:
"6........Negligence is omission of duty caused either by an omission to do something which a reasonable man guided upon those considerations who ordinarily by reason of conduct of human affairs would do or obligated to, or by doing something which a prudent or reasonable man would not do.

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Laxman Iyer and Another [2003 (8) SCC 731]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Negligence does not always mean absolute carelessness, but want of such a degree of care as is required in particular circumstances.

Negligence is failure to observe, for the protection of the interests of another person, the degree 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 of care,
precaution and vigilance which the circumstances justly demand, whereby such other person suffers injury.
The idea of negligence and duty are strictly correlative.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 Negligence means either subjectively a careless state of mind, or objectively careless conduct.
Negligence is not an absolute term, but is a relative one; it is rather a comparative term.
No absolute standard can be fixed and no mathematically exact formula can be laid down by which negligence or lack of it can be infallibly measured in a given case.

What constitutes negligence varies under different conditions and in determining whether negligence exists in a particular case, or whether a mere act or course of conduct amounts to negligence, all the attending and surrounding facts and circumstances have to be taken into account.
It is absence of care according to circumstances.
To determine whether an act would be or would not be negligent, it is relevant to determine if any reasonable man would foresee that the act would cause damage or not.
The omission to do what the law obligates or even the failure to do anything in a manner, mode or method envisaged by law would equally and per se constitute negligence on the part of such person.
If the answer is in the 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 affirmative, it is a negligent act.
Where an accident is due to negligence of both parties, substantially there would be contributory negligence and both would be blamed.

In a case of contributory negligence, the crucial question on which liability depends would be whether either party could, by exercise of reasonable care, have avoided the consequence of other's negligence.
...... Contributory negligence is applicable solely to the conduct of a plaintiff.

It means that there has been an act or omission on the part of the plaintiff which has materially contributed to the damage, the act or omission being of such a nature that it may properly be described as negligence, although negligence is not given its usual meaning.
........ It is now well settled that in the case of contributory negligence, courts have power to apportion the loss between the parties as seems just and equitable."
(Emphasis supplied)
A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investigation as to whether the deceased Milanth contributed to his own cause by failing to take the reasonable care.

It would be extremely difficult for the Tribunals and the Courts to define what would be the reasonable 2024:KER:75168 MACA NO. 212 OF 2021 care and would certainly depend upon the circumstances of each case.
9. In the present case, the duty of the driver of the vehicle bearing Regn. No.KL-7/AW-6586 was certainly on a higher pedestal compared to that of Milanth (deceased).
This Court is fortified in its view, especially when the Final Report of charge, Ext.A4, is perused.

In unequivocal terms, the charge sheet alleges a severe dereliction of duty on the side of driver of the vehicle bearing Regn.
No.KL-7/AW- 6586.
Merely because the deceased was driving the vehicle 5.15 meters away from its side of the road cannot by itself deem to a conclusion that he was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
It could be perhaps said that the deceased Milanth was overtaking another vehicle and thus had swerved 5.15 meters away from the road.

It must be noted that solely based on this finding in the final report, the insurance company is raising the contention that 75% of the contributory negligence ought to have been fixed against the deceased or at least 50% negligence should be attributed towards him.

sentences.text:
However, this Court is not impressed by the aforesaid contention in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Prem Lal Anand and Others v. Narendra Kumar and others [(2024)
SCC Online SC 1900], wherein it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court thus:
".. merely because a person was attempting to overtake a vehicle, cannot be said to be an act of rashness or negligence.."

entities.text:
Prem Lal Anand and Others v. Narendra Kumar and others [(2024)
SCC Online SC 1900]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The evidence on record does not persuade this Court to take a different view.
In fact, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal ought not to have fixed 25% negligence on the part of the deceased Milanth.
However, since, the claimants have not come up in appeal, this Court deems it appropriate not to deal with the aforesaid question.

11. On a cumulative assessment of the facts and also the evidence on record, this Court is not persuaded to overturn the findings rendered by the Motors Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam in the impugned award.
Hence, the appeal lacks merits and accordingly, the same is dismissed.
